Package neqsim.thermo.phase

Class PitzerParameterDatasets

java.lang.Object
neqsim.thermo.phase.PitzerParameterDatasets
public final class PitzerParameterDatasets extends Object
Coherent, versioned Pitzer parameter datasets whose equation conventions and public provenance have been mapped to PhasePitzer.

A dataset method configures only the named species system and marks that phase as manually populated so the legacy NeqSim table is not mixed into it. Additional active species remain subject to the normal fail-closed binary, mixed-ion, and neutral-family coverage diagnostics.

  • Method Details

    • applyPhreeqcCo2ChlorideParameters

      public static void applyPhreeqcCo2ChlorideParameters(PhasePitzer phase, Map<String,Double> co2ChlorideZeta)
      Applies PHREEQC Na/K/Ca/Mg chloride and CO2 lambda rows with caller-supplied constant zeta values.

      The bundled source has no explicit CO2-cation-Cl zeta rows. This method never supplies those missing values: callers must provide a finite value for every present cation, keyed by NeqSim ion name. A caller may explicitly adopt zero as a screening assumption, which is not an experimentally fitted interaction. All binary, theta, psi and lambda coefficients come from the pinned public-domain catalog without refitting. This is a manual, unqualified dataset; ordinary automatic catalog selection and its fail-closed policy are unchanged. Only water, CO2 and these four chloride salts are supported. Mixtures containing both K+ and Mg++ also lack a source theta row and require the overload with an explicit potassium-magnesium theta coefficient. Call on a fresh system after adding all components, before flashing or defining custom interaction families. This method overwrites the named rows, not unrelated custom interaction terms.

      Parameters:
      phase - Pitzer aqueous role
      co2ChlorideZeta - constant zeta for each present cation (Na+, K+, Ca++, Mg++)
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - for unsupported species, missing source rows or missing supplied zeta

    • applyPhreeqcCo2ChlorideParameters

      public static void applyPhreeqcCo2ChlorideParameters(PhasePitzer phase, Map<String,Double> co2ChlorideZeta, double potassiumMagnesiumTheta)
      Applies the chloride dataset with an explicit coefficient for the missing K+-Mg++ theta row.

      The supplied constant is used only when both ions are present. Like the supplied zeta values, a zero theta is an explicit screening assumption, not a fitted coefficient or a qualification of mixed brines.

      Parameters:
      phase - Pitzer aqueous role
      co2ChlorideZeta - constant zeta for each present cation
      potassiumMagnesiumTheta - finite constant K+-Mg++ theta in kg/mol
      See Also:
      • applyPhreeqcCo2ChlorideParameters(PhasePitzer, Map)

    • applyPhreeqcCo2SodiumSulfate

      public static void applyPhreeqcCo2SodiumSulfate(PhasePitzer phase)
      Applies the exact public-domain PHREEQC CO2-Na2SO4 parameter subset audited at commit b0b3be767158ccc3322d2c816625cf470045e67e, database blob 324f852784be84650b77bd7f07f8316aafd8188b.

      The configured molality-scale families are Na+/SO4-- beta0, beta1, and Cphi (PHREEQC C0); CO2/CO2, CO2/Na+, and CO2/SO4-- lambda; and CO2/Na+/SO4-- zeta. The 1-2 binary uses the standard alpha1=2 Pitzer branch and has no beta2 term. Values are passed in PHREEQC six-term order without fitting or conversion.

      Parameters:
      phase - Pitzer aqueous phase containing CO2, Na+, and SO4--
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a required component is absent or has the wrong charge role

    • applyPhreeqcSodiumPotassiumChloride

      public static void applyPhreeqcSodiumPotassiumChloride(PhasePitzer phase)
      Applies the coherent public-domain PHREEQC Na-K-Cl parameter subset audited at commit b0b3be767158ccc3322d2c816625cf470045e67e, database blob 324f852784be84650b77bd7f07f8316aafd8188b.

      The subset contains the complete binary B0, B1, and C0 six-term temperature functions for Na+/Cl- and K+/Cl-, the K+/Na+ theta interaction, and the Cl-/K+/Na+ psi six-term function. PHREEQC C0 maps directly to NeqSim Cphi before the common charge normalization. Both binaries use alpha1=2; neither has a B2 term. Values are passed without fitting, scale conversion, or mixing with the legacy NeqSim dataset.

      Parameters:
      phase - Pitzer aqueous phase containing Na+, K+, and Cl-
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a required component is absent or has the wrong charge role

    • tryApplyCompletePhreeqcPitzerCatalog

      public static boolean tryApplyCompletePhreeqcPitzerCatalog(PhasePitzer phase)
      Tries to apply every explicit PHREEQC row required by the active aqueous topology.

      Validation completes before any phase mutation. Hydrocarbons are excluded because they remain on the EOS gas/oil role phases; non-hydrocarbon aqueous neutrals still require complete lambda and zeta coverage. A missing source row returns false, allowing the caller to retain the legacy single-salt dataset. Mixed legacy topologies still fail through the ordinary coverage gate rather than receiving silent zero interactions.

      Parameters:
      phase - Pitzer aqueous role
      Returns:
      true when the complete source topology was found and applied

    • applyCompletePhreeqcPitzerCatalog

      public static void applyCompletePhreeqcPitzerCatalog(PhasePitzer phase)
      Applies every explicit PHREEQC Pitzer row required by the phase's active species topology.

      The exact public-domain source catalog is loaded lazily. Opposite-sign ion pairs require explicit B0, B1, and C0 rows; same-sign pairs require THETA; mixed-ion triples require PSI; and active neutral solutes require all applicable LAMBDA and ZETA rows. An absent required row fails before the phase is mutated. B2 is applied when explicitly present, including PHREEQC's 2-1 CaCl2 term. Thus catalog breadth never turns an unqualified omitted coefficient into a silent zero.

      Parameters:
      phase - Pitzer aqueous phase whose active species define the requested catalog subset
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a required explicit source row is absent

    • isHydrocarbonForAutomaticCatalog

      static boolean isHydrocarbonForAutomaticCatalog(ComponentInterface component)
      Identifies EOS-role hydrocarbons without relying only on the mutable component-type flag.

      Normal database components such as methane can retain component type normal in a GE phase. Their molecular formula remains an unambiguous discriminator: a pure hydrocarbon contains carbon and hydrogen only. Explicit neutral Pitzer datasets are unaffected; this helper is used only by automatic catalog selection.

    • getQualification

      public static PitzerParameterQualification getQualification(String datasetId)
      Returns reviewed scientific qualification metadata for a named built-in dataset.

      Complete interaction coverage does not imply experimental qualification. In particular, the broad PHREEQC catalog has exact public-domain source provenance while only named subsystems have independent experimental evidence. Unknown/manual identities fail closed as PitzerParameterQualification.Level.UNQUALIFIED.

      Parameters:
      datasetId - stable dataset identity reported by PhasePitzer.getParameterDatasetId()
      Returns:
      immutable qualification metadata

    • isWithinStrontiumChlorideValidationRange

      public static boolean isWithinStrontiumChlorideValidationRange(double temperature, double strontiumChlorideMolality)
      Reports whether an SrCl2 state is inside the independent NIST ThermoML validation envelope.

      The archive contains 22 values at 298.15 K from 0.01 to 3.52 mol/kg and 36 temperature-dependent values from 283.15 to 333.15 K at 0.01 to 0.30 mol/kg. This helper describes the enclosing rectangle; callers needing the exact measured state set must consult the stored validation fixture.

      Parameters:
      temperature - temperature in K
      strontiumChlorideMolality - SrCl2 formula-unit molality in mol/kg water
      Returns:
      true for finite states inside the inclusive validation envelope

    • isWithinCalciumMagnesiumChlorideMixtureValidationRange

      public static boolean isWithinCalciumMagnesiumChlorideMixtureValidationRange(double temperature, double calciumChlorideMolality, double magnesiumChlorideMolality)
      Reports whether a mixed CaCl2-MgCl2 state is inside the independently checked isopiestic envelope.

      The public-domain NBS evidence covers 298.15 K, total formula-unit molality 0.548-2.161 mol/kg water, and CaCl2 fractions 0.25-0.75. This helper describes that rectangular evidence envelope; it does not qualify sulfate-bearing mixtures or extrapolation beyond the underlying three isopiestic levels.

      Parameters:
      temperature - temperature in K
      calciumChlorideMolality - CaCl2 formula-unit molality in mol/kg water
      magnesiumChlorideMolality - MgCl2 formula-unit molality in mol/kg water
      Returns:
      true for finite, non-negative inputs inside the checked mixed-chloride envelope

    • isWithinMagnesiumChlorideSulfateWaterActivityValidationRange

      public static boolean isWithinMagnesiumChlorideSulfateWaterActivityValidationRange(double temperature, double magnesiumChlorideMolality, double magnesiumSulfateMolality)
      Reports whether a mixed MgCl2-MgSO4 state is inside the independently checked water-activity envelope.

      The evidence contains three composition lines at MgCl2 ionic-strength fractions 0.20, 0.50, and 0.80. The line-specific total formula-unit molality ranges are 0.60-2.96, 0.35-3.50, and 0.95-3.80 mol/kg water, respectively. The small fraction tolerance represents the source table's two-decimal composition rounding; this method does not qualify interpolation between the three composition lines.

      Parameters:
      temperature - temperature in K
      magnesiumChlorideMolality - MgCl2 formula-unit molality in mol/kg water
      magnesiumSulfateMolality - MgSO4 formula-unit molality in mol/kg water
      Returns:
      true for finite, non-negative inputs on a checked composition line and inside its molality range
